$comment: Sample settings for crew-for-claude. The hook wiring is the important part — it makes the git/secrets backstop fire on every Bash call and the secret backstop fire on every file write. Adjust permissions to your comfort: the example below is a dev-phase posture (broad allow + a hard hook backstop). Narrow the allow list before any deployed environment.

permissions.$comment_permissions: Start strict and add what you trust, OR run a broad allow during heavy dev (e.g. "Bash(*)", "Write(*)") RELYING ON the hooks below as the real backstop. The hooks block irreversible ops and secret writes regardless of the allow list.

hooks.$comment_sessionstart: The onboarding + freshness SENSORS (Loops 1 and 3; see docs/adr/0002). onboard.sh fires on a FRESH/un-installed repo and surfaces the right 'install -> alive' offer per folder shape (empty / single repo / multi-repo); it goes silent once the crew is installed AND CONTEXT.md is authored. check-freshness.sh fires on an ALREADY-installed+oriented repo and nudges toward drift-audit when CONTEXT.md looks stale vs the code (cheap git-commit-count heuristic). Both are read-only, never block, fail silent. Their actuators are /orient and drift-audit respectively.

hooks.$comment_attribution: Blocks vendor/model-tier names on the git surface (commit messages) when attributionTrailer is configured in skills-config.json. Default OFF (no-op) when attributionTrailer is empty.

PreToolUse.$comment_read: Path-safety on the Read surface: block-path-escape.sh stops an absolute-path Read into a sibling repo (the cross-repo hole the cwd-only block-cd-escape.sh cannot reach). Tunable via PATH_ALLOWED_ROOTS.

hooks.$comment_memsize: Keeps each .claude/memory/*.md under ~24KB. Over the ceiling it blocks the write and instructs the agent to compress/consolidate older records (or split a topic out) THEN re-write — 'make room, then continue', not a hard stop. Tunable via MEMORY_MAX_BYTES / MEMORY_WARN_BYTES.

hooks.$comment_pathescape: Path-safety on the write surface: blocks an absolute-path Write/Edit into a sibling repo. Tunable via PATH_ALLOWED_ROOTS.

hooks.$comment_arch: Architecture-violation guard. arch-patterns.example.sh ships EMPTY (a safe no-op) — a consumer fills it with their CLAUDE.md auto-fail regexes (rename to arch-patterns.sh). Until filled it blocks nothing.

PreToolUse.$comment_lane: Agent lane discipline (see .claude/memory/agent-lane-discipline.md): block spawning the orchestrator (lead-agent) as a sub-agent — it self-blocks on nested Task/Bash and wastes tokens. Orchestration is done by the main session; only domain leads/workers are spawnable.

hooks.$comment_drift_dormant: DORMANT ON PURPOSE: .claude/hooks/check-doctrine-drift.sh ships but is intentionally NOT wired below. Once wired it BLOCKS any workflow whose inlined _doctrine.js canonical region drifts — but the existing crew workflows don't yet inline the region (the retrofit is pending). Wire it (a Write|Edit|MultiEdit PreToolUse entry) ONLY after every workflow inlines the region, else editing them bricks.
hooks.$comment_posttooluse: Advisory nudges (never block; always exit 0). post-edit-nudges.sh nudges on missing-test-companion / stale-CONTEXT after a code edit; handoff-threshold-nudge.sh nudges a long-running lead toward /context-handoff at safe thresholds.
hooks.$comment_stop: The learning loop's SENSOR. suggest-memory.sh fires when the main agent finishes a turn, reads the last user message from the transcript, and — if it looks like a durable lesson (a correction, a 'from now on', a locked decision, a preference) — surfaces a one-line nudge to run /remember. It NEVER writes and NEVER blocks; it only notices. /remember (the skill) is the write half, and it proposes every version-controlled edit before making it. Together they are the back-flow that makes the crew auto-grow.
hooks.$comment_packs: When a pack is activated (e.g. python-fastapi), the installer adds that pack's hooks here too. The python-fastapi pack adds a Bash-matcher entry for .claude/hooks/enforce-venv.sh (copied from packs/python-fastapi/hooks/ on activation). That hook enforces the crew's Python venv rule: ONE .venv at the repo root and EVERY Python command (pip/python/pytest/mypy/…) runs inside it — bare system-interpreter commands are blocked. This kit repo has no Python project code of its own, so the entry is not added here; the moment Python is added (here or in any consumer), /install (or a hand-add of the entry below) turns it on.
